title: New work order shows Sales Representative under Service Advisor as Unassigned
custom_preconds:
Objective

Check that a new work order whose customer has no sales representative shows the Sales Representative field directly under Service Advisor, reading "Unassigned", as plain text when the mouse is not over it.

  • Scenario: You open a new work order for a customer who has no sales representative and look at the card.

Test data (create these in the account first)

  • {Location-A}: a location of your shop where you are signed in with the Admin role.
    For example: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • {Customer-A}: a customer with no sales representative (in Edit Customer, its Sales Representative field reads "Unassigned").
    For example: ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • {Work-order-1}: a work order created for {Customer-A} at {Location-A}, not invoiced or paid, on which nobody has picked a sales representative.
    For example: S2-40001.

Before you start

  • You are signed in with the Admin role at {Location-A}.
  • You are on the Work Orders page, on a desktop or laptop computer with a mouse (not a phone or a touch screen).
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open work order {Work-order-1} from the Work Orders list.
  2. Move the mouse pointer to an empty part of the page, away from the work order card.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the work order opens. On the card, a field labelled "Sales Representative" sits directly under Service Advisor. (Lead Technician may read blank; that is today's behaviour and not part of this test.)
  • Step 2: the field reads "Sales Representative" on the first line and "Unassigned" on the second, in the same text style, size and boldness as Service Advisor and starting at the same left edge. There is no box around it, no dropdown arrow and no button beside it, as in the attached picture of board 1.2.

Pass: both steps show exactly what is described above. Fail: anything differs (for example the field is missing, sits elsewhere, reads a name, or shows a box, arrow or button at rest); write down the step number and attach a screenshot of the card.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 13 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11265 (Story 1, Give a work order its sales representative), story SV-11268 (Story 4, Give a customer default representatives)

  • Story 1 prerequisite: “User has 'Work Orders — Create & Edit' enabled.”
  • Story 1 prerequisite: “The work order is not invoiced or paid, and is not opened from its history.”
  • S1-R1: “The work order card shows a Sales Representative field directly under Service Advisor.”
  • S1-R2: “The field is the same field as Lead Technician and Service Advisor: the label "Sales Representative" sits inside it on the first line and the name on the second, in the same text style, size, weight and left edge.”
  • S1-R3: “At rest the field shows no box, no dropdown arrow and no buttons beside it.”
  • S1-R7: “With nobody assigned, the field reads "Unassigned".”
  • S4-R24: “A new work order for a customer that is not split starts with the customer's representative in its one Sales Representative field. The work order is not split.”
  • S3-R4: “Nothing in the fields or the buttons depends on hover. On a touch screen the Sales Representative fields always show their dropdown arrow, as the + and remove x buttons always do. Lead Technician and Service Advisor keep today's behavior, where the arrow shows once the field is tapped.”

From: Tech plan "Splitting Sales Representatives — Technical Implementation Plan" (dated 14 Oct 2026, planned against PRD version 8; uploaded 19 Oct 2026 and again, byte-identical, 22 Oct 2026), read in full 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan, Already built: “Already built: the work order's single rep field with "Unassigned", (Inactive), save-as-you-go and the read-only gate (SV-8599)”
